newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds end higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds end higher in thin trade.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds closed higher in thin and directionless trading on Monday in the run-up to the the Bank of Israel's announcement on interest rates, traders said.
At the end of the trading day the Bank of Israel said it was lowering its key lending rate for January by 0.5 percentage point to an annualised 14.7 percent.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 172.86
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 162.8
Volume was a low 109 million shekels with activity in unlinked bonds falling to only 23 million shekels.
"Investors were waiting for the rate decision as the market lost direction. Bonds prices are expected to rise on Tuesday following the rate cut," said Baruch Glicksberg of Clal Insurance.
CPI-linked bonds were very mixed with slightly higher demand for short bonds, said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.
Unlinked bonds and Makams continued to rise but volume fell. "The main buyers were investors who expected a rate cut of around 0.5 point," Glicksberg said.

Dollar-linked bonds closed lower, but traders said the bonds were expected to begin rising on Tuesday following the rate decision. "The shekel started declining against the dollar after the rate announcement and is expected continue its decline on Tuesday," Gliksberg said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
